itineraries.title: Rangpur City Weekend
itineraries.subtitle: Palace, college lawns & Begum Rokeya's village
itineraries.seasonNote: Comfortable any season; coolest and clearest Oct–Feb.
itineraries.summary: A relaxed two-day dip into Rangpur city's finest: the Indo-European Tajhat Palace and the vast Carmichael College campus on day one, followed by a half-day run out to the quiet village of Payrabondh where Begum Rokeya was born.

stops.name: Tajhat Palace (Rangpur Museum)
stops.note: explore the ornate marble staircase and museum galleries

stops.name: Carmichael College
stops.note: stroll the century-old campus grounds and Victorian-era main building

stops.name: Begum Rokeya Memorial Centre, Payrabondh (Mithapukur)
stops.note: pay respects at the birth home and interpretive centre of the pioneer educationist

stops.name: Mithapukur Mosque
stops.note: a graceful local mosque worth a brief stop on the return to town

itineraries.title: North Bengal Heritage Loop
itineraries.subtitle: Terracotta temples, palaces & old estates
itineraries.seasonNote: Cool, dry touring weather across the north.
itineraries.summary: Four days tracing the finest princely and religious architecture of northern Bangladesh — from Rangpur's Italianate palace to Dinajpur's terracotta masterpiece and the mango-tree estate of Thakurgaon.

stops.name: Tajhat Palace (Rangpur Museum)
stops.note: the city's centrepiece — budget two hours for the palace and its museum

stops.name: Carmichael College
stops.note: an evening walk through one of the oldest colleges in Bengal

stops.name: Kantajew Temple
stops.note: the finest terracotta temple in Bangladesh — arrive early to beat the crowds

stops.name: Dinajpur Rajbari
stops.note: a sprawling 18th-century estate; explore the outer courts and pond

stops.name: Ramsagar National Park
stops.note: the largest man-made lake in Bangladesh, ideal for a quiet morning walk

stops.name: Suryapuri Mango Tree of Harinmari (Baliadangi)
stops.note: the legendary centuries-old mango tree — a singular sight in open farmland

stops.name: Jamalpur Zamindar Bari Jame Mosque
stops.note: a well-preserved mosque attached to a former zamindar estate

itineraries.title: Far-North Frontier & Hills
itineraries.subtitle: Kanchenjunga views, tea & the Teesta
itineraries.seasonNote: Go on a clear winter dawn for the mountain view from Tetulia.
itineraries.summary: An active four-day sweep of Bangladesh's northernmost extremities — Himalayan views at dawn from Tetulia, an ancient fort city buried in fields, the world's largest mango tree, and the geopolitical curiosity of the Tin Bigha Corridor by the Teesta Barrage.

stops.name: Kanchenjunga View from Tetulia
stops.note: rise before dawn for the clearest Himalayan skyline in Bangladesh

stops.name: Banglabandha Zero Point
stops.note: stand at the northernmost tip of Bangladesh at the India–Nepal tri-junction

stops.name: Bhitargarh Fort City
stops.note: explore the massive earthen ramparts of a pre-medieval fortified city

stops.name: Tetulia Tea Gardens
stops.note: walk the rows of Bangladesh's northernmost tea garden in the afternoon light

stops.name: Suryapuri Mango Tree of Harinmari (Baliadangi)
stops.note: the famous centuries-old mango tree that sprawls over nearly an acre

stops.name: Tin Bigha Corridor & Dahagram–Angarpota
stops.note: walk the narrow land corridor connecting the Bangladeshi enclave — a unique geopolitical site

stops.name: Teesta Barrage at Doani (Hatibandha)
stops.note: the major river barrage controlling Teesta irrigation; fine views at dusk
